newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end mixed ahead of CPI.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end mixed ahead of CPI.

text.p: Israeli shares closed mixed on Thursday in active and selective trading ahead of the release of the April consumer price index (CPI), traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 0.09 percent, or 0.24 points, to 264.11 on a high all-share turnover of 160 million shekels against 118 million shekels on Wednesday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index closed 0.37 percent lower at 271.33.

The April CPI, released after the end of the trading day rose 0.7 percent. The figure was lower than market expectations of a 1.1 percent rise. Traders said that the surprising CPI will have a positive impact when trading resumes on Sunday.
"The CPI was surprisingly low and the options (market today) reflects hopes for a substantial rise on Sunday," said Shahar Gazit of Betucha Securities and Investments.
"Now the Bank of Israel may decide to lower its key lending rate, but it won't lower it by more than half-a-percentage point," he said.
The central bank last cut its key rate at the end of February to 13.9 percent.

"Activity was very high today and the fact that so many shares changed hands is very positive. Trading was very mixed today as the Maof index gets closer to 278 (its all time high set on February 18)," said Eli Nahum, head of trading at Zannex Securities.

"As we get closer to the 278 barrier some investors get nervous and start selling but the positive factor is that there are enough buyers that believe that the bullish trend will continue," Nahum added.

Gazit added that the selective trading indicated that investors show more interest in the market. "Prices rose sharply and now the activity is also rising. This is a clear indication that the market is becoming more interesting".

Dead Sea Works DESA.TA lost 0.5 percent to 1,156 agorot. The company said on Thursday that net profit in the first quarter of 1997 rose to 37.4 million shekels from 35.5 million shekels a year earlier.

The most active share was Teva Pharmaceutical Industries, which surged 3.75 percent to 20,097 agorot on turnover of 15.6 million shekels. Teva rose after its ADR traded on Nasdaq rose 4.1 percent on Wednesday.

Other active shares included Israel Chemicals, which gained 0.75 percent to 396 agorot on turnover of 11.4 million shekels and Israel Discount Bank, which rose 0.5 percent to 363 on volume of 10 million shekels.
